Subject: Competitive intel & QBR prep: pricing moves, model releases, and OKR asks

Team — sharing a concise intel pack ahead of QBR prep. Extracted the field notes from Sales, Product triage, and a couple of customers. High-level bullets and asks below; full attachments are included.

Key points:
- Nebula (competitor) rolled out a time-limited enterprise credit program (50% off first-year committed spend) targeting SMB -> mid-market deals. Early signals: a couple of engaged FinTech prospects have pushed procurement conversations to see if Nebula's credits can be matched.
- Atlas-AI announced a 16k-context model variant and a new SLO tier for reduced-latency edge instances. Pricing tier appears optimized for token-heavy retrieval apps.
- Marketplace: one of our channel partners reported Nebula and Atlas offering expedited onboarding via marketplace credits and a pre-configured VPC template. This lowers friction and shortens procurement cycles.
- Product impact: Atlas's 16k model makes them more competitive on long-context summarization and retrieval augmentation; Nebula's credit offering is pricing-first.

Immediate asks for QBR slides (due next WED):
1) Ops/Cost impact slide — show how competitor credits change unit economics for typical mid-market deal (ask: Sales ops + Finance to provide 3 example deal trims).
2) Feature differentiation slide — call out where our runtime/observability/rollouts reduce MTTR and total cost vs competitors (Product to draft one pager).
3) Risk slide — list accounts in churn/at-risk because of competitor credits (CS + AE to confirm).

Attachments: competitor-pricing-summary.csv (sales-derived), model-release-timeline.pdf (public blog + internal notes).

I'll consolidate notes into a single QBR deck draft and share a slot for a leadership review on Friday. Please respond with the owner for the three asks above and any missing intel by EOD Monday.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Folks — some strategy thoughts to include in the QBR slide deck:

1) Counter-credit play: offer a short-term onboarding credit tied to committed usage but structured as a performance rebate (pay-for-performance) rather than a blunt upfront credit. This preserves margin while addressing procurement psychology.
2) Product can accelerate a canary for a lower-latency deployment path (targeted at customers with token-heavy pipelines) — label this as an official "16k-context partner path" so we can market parity with Atlas on long context use cases.
3) Emphasize our observability/rollout features in the sales playbook: show an example where our rollback + tracing saved a production customer 4 hours of downtime vs competitor.

I recommend we capture the proposed counter-credit mechanics as a single slide and include a short appendix with the canary timeline.

Linking HubSpot deal for context: https://hubspot.company.com/deal/HS-4892

-Karthik
